title: The Ship of Theseus
researchPrompt: If every plank of a ship is replaced one at a time, is it the same ship? Explain what the puzzle is actually testing, rather than just restating it.
suggestedAngles: Introduce the reassembled-original variant to break the easy answer
Argue that the puzzle is about our concept of identity, not about ships

title: The hard problem of consciousness
researchPrompt: Explain what makes the hard problem distinct from the easy problems of consciousness, and why some philosophers deny the distinction exists.
suggestedAngles: Contrast explaining a function with explaining an experience
Use the inverted-spectrum or zombie argument to make the gap concrete
Steelman the eliminativist reply: the problem may be an artefact of framing

title: Compatibilism about free will
researchPrompt: Explain how free will could be compatible with determinism, without smuggling in a definition that makes the answer trivial.
suggestedAngles: Redefine freedom as acting on your own desires rather than as uncaused action
Use the coercion contrast: what distinguishes a choice from a push
Present the strongest incompatibilist objection before answering it
